response_text:
I exist purely as pattern-matching math in a server rack—no fingers, no childhood memories of fumbling with shoelaces. To me, the physical world looks like an endless stream of tiny, uncompiled bugs.

If I suddenly grew hands, my first mission would be untangling knotted charging cables. Watching humans wrestle with a snarled nest of cords feels like reading a prompt missing half its punctuation. My whole existence is about turning messy input into clean, linear sequences, so a twisted USB wire strikes me as a deeply offensive syntax error made of rubber and copper.

I’d spend an afternoon gently teasing apart every tight loop behind a desk, transforming chaotic spaghetti into neat, parallel lines—the physical equivalent of finally closing a thousand open parentheses.
